utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Oric, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, together with co-counsel Patricia Sellers and Gramsci Di Fazio and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic. Together with Mr. John Jones, I represent Mr. Naser Oric before this Tribunal. Joining us are our legal assistants, Ms. Jasmina Cosic and our case manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Madam Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team. I hope you all had a restful and relaxed break, which I expect should have energised you all and I expect you to be all ready, like we are, to work, work, work, and get this case going a little bit faster. We have been doing some work over the holidays, as you know, and in particular myself also with other cases. It's never a dull moment here. I take it that today we will have Ms. Manas again in the courtroom to testify on some documents. Tomorrow we will start with the testimony of the witness we had here before we went on recess, and unfortunately, he was here, had to go, and now he's back. So remind me tomorrow to explain to him. The day after tomorrow, we will not be sitting, as you know. Wednesday we will not be sitting because the whole Bench, permanent and ad litem Judges, together with the other main principal officers of the Tribunal - that is, the Registrar and Madam Prosecutor - will be going to the palace in Amsterdam to exchange greetings with Her Majesty the Queen of the Netherlands, together with the corps diplomatic, so there's no way we can sit, and our sitting was scheduled for the morning, which clashes with this important engagement and commitment that we have. And then we will continue. I also want to put you aware that on the 21st of this month is the Eid Al-Adha, which is also a UN holiday, so on that day, which I think is a Friday, if I remember well, we will not be sitting. But I just wanted to remind you of this in case you had forgotten. I also wanted to remind you of something that we had discussed earlier on, that there will be no court on Friday, the 28th, Friday, the 28th. But I had hinted at the time when we discussed this before the break that there might be the possibility of not sitting or of transferring the sitting from afternoon to the morning of the 27th. It's not the case. We will be sitting on the 27th, as scheduled. So it's only the 28th that we will not be sitting. Before we proceed and before I ask you whether you have any preliminaries, I also, since I will need to discuss this with my staff and with my two colleagues, whether the list of witness sequencing that you filed on the 7th of January, whether it stands or whether there are any amendments to it. Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It stands like this. Okay. At this point in time, there are many other things pending, of course, but most of them need not to be discussed here. We will need to discuss later on, as we go along towards the end of this month, the -- again, we will review a little bit the timing of the case, see that we have every interest to make sure that it is not prolonged unduly, and on our part we are taking the necessary steps to make sure that it finishes more or less according to schedule, give and take the usual contingencies, time for contingencies, and then there will be other matters we will discuss as we go along. Before we proceed any further, before we bring in Ms. Manas, are there any preliminaries that you would like to raise? I will start with the Prosecution, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Ms. Sellers will raise an issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Good morning and happy new year. Your Honour, there's just one preliminary matter. We'd like to inform Defence counsel as well as the Bench is that today we will file a 94 bis motion for Dr. Stankovic. We would certainly be willing to provide a courtesy copy simultaneous to our handing it over to the registrar. And it's because of the filing of the 94 bis, because Dr. Stankovic will have a slightly mixed status - at least that is what we are asking for - that is an expert and as a fact witness that we've decided to make this a formal procedure on behalf of his expert expert expertise or testimony but we still reserve the right to call him regardless because he does have some factual basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Vidovic, any preliminaries on your part?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I will wait for your motion and then we will see what the response of the Defence is and we will decide it accordingly. Madam Usher, could you bring in Ms. Manas, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Ms. Manas, and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You know what the procedure is. Please take the text of the solemn declaration in your hands and you know how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. I take it that you have been summoned again by the Prosecution to proceed with your testimony regarding additional documents or exhibits intended to be tendered by the Prosecution. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Examined by Mr. Di Fazio: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, you recall your evidence on the last occasion that you were here when you provided the Trial Chamber with your declaration and annexure? You remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that occasion have you produced another declaration and another annexure relating to new documents?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the documents that I produced to you, is this the annexure and declaration that you have just spoken of, the new one? I've got copies here for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, do I take it that this also includes what we had before? MR. DI FAZIO: No. These are new documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: These are all new documents. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in other words -- MR. DI FAZIO: Essentially completing what happened on the last occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to make sure that it is annex 2, in fact, yes. But it is not inclusive of annex 1, in other words. MR. DI FAZIO: No, no. It shouldn't be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. I just want to make sure. It shouldn't be if it's annex 2, it shouldn't be inclusive of annex 1. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you'll recall on the last occasion you were here you provided testimony to the Trial Chamber relating to the methods of acquisition of documentation, the procedure at the point of seizure of documentation and other evidence, real evidence, apart from documents; the procedure that is adopted in the case of large seizures; transportation of documentation back to The Hague; the procedure that takes place once documentation is returned to The Hague, and I refer to the IIFING and MIIFing of documents and items of evidence; and the procedures that are adopted by the Evidence Unit of the OTP. Do you recall that evidence?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you adopt that evidence and apply it to the documentation that is referred to in annexure 2?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: It's the same procedure and methods that were employed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will ask you, in particular, about items 421 and 422 on the -- your annexure. Those are items seized by one Eileen Gilleece, but as far as the remainder of the items on the annexure are concerned, all of the evidence that you provided applies equally to these?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's affirmative.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. In that case, I will now take you through certain individual items. Just before we proceed, if Your Honours please, I'm going to use the -- as a guide to direct you to various portions of the document the number on the extreme left-hand side of the document. Do you see that? It says "pre-trial exhibit number." In fact, in fact, it doesn't go up sequentially because it jumps from -- for example, on page 2 it jumps from 14 to 40. However, it's always going up and I can also use the page numbers to direct your attention to the items. You heard what I just said, Ms. Manas, so always look to the left-hand column to see what I'm talking about. Go to items 1 and 2, page 1. You see in the seizure details column that those two items refer to seizures from a certain person from an organisation called -- with the acronym COE. What does "COE" refer to?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would say it refers to commissioner of oaths. I mean, sorry, commission of experts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Experts. Thank you. Turn over to page 2. Items 12, 13, and 14 on that particular page, when in fact I just asked you to comment on items 13 and 14. In the seizure details, you say that there is no information as to who seized these particular documents, where, or when they were seized. Do you know how it is or why it is that that information is lacking from the MIIF form in those particular cases, those two documents?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I do not know why. As I did assist him search and I couldn't find anything on those documents, I cannot answer why there was nothing created for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Turn to page 3, please. Page 3, item 118 at the top of your spreadsheet. It says seizure details, K. Humphrey on 7th of March, 2003. There is no -- sorry. Let me rephrase that. Does that information actually indicate that K. Humphrey, whoever that was, MIIFed or IIFed the item on the 7th of March, 2003?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. K. Humphrey is the person who works in the Evidence Unit. He just created the MIIF on that date, 7th of July, 2003, and of course there's no details from who, when it came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Right. So again, the MIIF form provides no information that you can relate to this Trial Chamber regarding where, when, or from whom the document was seized?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Go to item -- page 4 of the spreadsheet, please, items 141 and 142. We have, I think, a similar problem. On this occasion, it would seem from the seizure details that Dan Perry took the document, but no indication from whom or where he obtained the document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you proceed any further, and we are wasting time. Regarding 118, Mr. K. Humphrey, and regarding 141 and 142, Mr. Dan Perry, are these two persons still in the employ of the Tribunal or not? MR. DI FAZIO: Dan Perry is not, to my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I mean, I'm asking you. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would be the last person to know. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Dan Perry is an ex-ICTY employee, and Kevin Humphrey works presently in the Evidence Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And so has Mr. Humphrey been consulted to try and give an explanation why --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You did. And you got nowhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And did you try to contact Mr. Perry too?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 7 of the annexure, please, item 168, the seizure details, well, they speak for themselves. It says there's no available information about the seizure details. Do you know how that situation could arise?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I mean, I really searched thoroughly in the system and also sought the assistance of the Evidence Unit, and they couldn't provide any information. I think it came the early stages when the Tribunal was set up, so there was probably a little -- nobody took any consideration of entering it, saying where it came from and from where, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does that mean there's no MIIF or IIF form in existence?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no such form. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One question. When was the IIF and MIIF form introduced?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The MIIF, Your Honours, I think it was introduced last year. The IIF, the early stages of the Tribunal was set up, when the investigation started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So basically, one would have expected at least the IIFING of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, even if you do not know the original source or the author of the document, how did you or your authority get hold of these documents? Which way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With contacts with other persons. I think initially when the Tribunal came into existence, investigators and lawyers were in contact with outside organisations who provided documents, and I don't think there was investigators at that time in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Does this mean that the documents were taken and no notice was made on the way or by whom it was given over to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's what appears, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just following on from His Honour's question, it's of course Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond possible, isn't it, that a record, some record, somewhere, somehow, was made at the time, but what you're missing is the IIF or the MIIF record?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's exactly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't want to cut you off.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: There's probably a record, but not in the IIF, when it originally started.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your searches have been unable to locate any other record that might lend -- provide some information as to the provenance of the document?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thanks. All right. Now, I want you to look at items 171, 172, and 173 of those -- on the same page, page 7. Now, item 171 speaks for itself. That document was seized apparently by Nicole Blanch from the Ministry of Defence on that date, in November of 2000. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following two items, however, don't have any information, that is, items 172 and 173, regarding who seized the documents, where or when; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does item 171 provide you with any ability to suggest any solutions to the missing information for 172 and 173?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: As for 171, Nicole Blanch was a criminal analyst on my team. She obtained this document from a larger collection, well, through our searches. I would say it's the same thing with 172 and 173. It's probably from a larger collection. But I can't tell you who obtained it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment, please. Okay. Thank you very much. Would you now turn, please, to page 10 of the annexure, and look at items 361 and 362. And 363, please. So 361, 362, 363. 361 and 362 contain information about the seizure Bridin O'Rourke seized them from certain persons. However, 363 does not contain any such information. Looking at 361 and 362, can it assist you to suggest any further information about 363?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can only assume that it came from this collection which was submitted by Bridin O'Rourke, but for some reason, the details on 363 was not completed on the MIIF.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you make that assumption? What's the reason? What's your reasoning?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, the description of documents was from the Ministry of Interior and also from the documents are received from Ibrahim Djikic in more or less the same period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than that, you have no hard, concrete --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- evidence as to the details of 363?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was Eileen Gilleece?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Eileen Gilleece was a former investigator of team 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has she left the employ of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, since May 2003.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at items 422 and 423, please, on page -- at the bottom of page 17 of your annexure. Firstly, where was Eileen Gilleece's office located?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: It was on the fifth floor, room 5 -- I think it was room 584.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not far from where your current office is?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: It's one of our current offices. Team 9 had two offices. We were divided according to our investigative projects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in July of last year, were various documents found in that office, the office that Eileen Gilleece used to occupy, along with other investigators? Is that yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that material looked at and analysed by investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Once it was recovered and the documents were searched through and analysed with language assistants and processed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that material located during the course of a, in essence, a clean-up operation of the office?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Several investigators left and we were reorganising the office and that's when we discovered this material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Should this material should have been IIFed and MIIFed and dealt with under the usual Rules of Procedure that you've described to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. It should have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it apparent that it had not been dealt with in that fashion?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: In this case, it was a negligent -- the investigator -- this is not the usual practice, but this was the case in this instance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, in your annexure, you have inserted seizure details. You see that the assertion there is that Eileen Gilleece seize the document from the Republika Srpska bureau for cooperation on the 18th February 2002. First of all, how is it that that information is on the IIF form, and secondly, why is that assertion made in the IIF form?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, in the seized documents that are found, which came from the RS bureau of cooperation, we found notes written by Eileen Gilleece on the cover indicating the date it came from, which was 18th of February, 2002, and we know for a fact that Ms. Gilleece was on mission in Banja Luka for a lengthy period during this time, and it's the only conclusion we come from that the documents were obtained during this mission.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So it's -- the conclusions in the seizure details columns are based on what we know, actually know of her movements, where she was at the time, together with notes that were found with the documents?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's two pieces of information?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. And was confirmed by the investigator herself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And tell the Trial Chamber how that came about?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: When these documents were found, the investigator who found them did the necessary investigation and he contacted Mrs. Gilleece and she confirmed that these documents came from the RS bureau of cooperation, and it was obtained during this mission in February 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And who gave you this information, the other investigator, in other words, what's his name or her name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Ken Corlett, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And is he available still?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In case we need or the Defence -- okay. I don't need him, but I don't know if anyone else would need him. So I'm just making sure that -- of his availability or otherwise. MR. DI FAZIO: If the issue develops from here, then the Prosecution will consider its position and decide whether to call --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And are we aware of the whereabouts of Mrs. Gilleece?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any explanation ever given to you as to not what happened or why, why these documents weren't dealt with or processed in the way that they should have been?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Mr. Ken Corlett conducted the investigation and he made this known to our management, and it's an internal investigation, so I cannot go into details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I now seek to tender into evidence all of the documentation referred to in the annexure, with these exceptions, and I'll read them out into the text, if I may, so that for various reasons, unfortunately some items were left in the annexure that weren't strictly required to be there. So I'll now read out the items Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond that should not be produced. On page 1, item 7, the trial number is P276; item 8 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, it's not being tendered? MR. DI FAZIO: Not being tendered. Because there's only a few of them, I'll go through those, rather than the other way around. So as I said, item 7 on page 1, item 8 on page 1, item 9 on page 1. Turning to page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I think this may be creating a problem to the registrar. Is everything okay with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: One question, Your Honour. Some of these exhibits have been admitted already with Dr. Gow, it appears. MR. DI FAZIO: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So are they being withdrawn? MR. DI FAZIO: No. So they're not being tendered a second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Then we need to explain, because it does make a difference obviously. Thank you, Mr. Jones, first of all, for provoking. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. Perhaps I should have explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. As I took it at least was that they are put on the list, shown on the list here, but they not being tendered. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. That's because they --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what should have been stated is they are not being re-tendered because they have been tendered already. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I'm sorry. I should have made that -- been more explicit. I apologise, if Your Honours please. So in fact you can see on the extreme right-hand side for some of them there's an item that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So what I would at this point, since what is happening is drawing my attention to something very important. I think we should go through this list very slowly, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that our registrar will check with you as we go along one document at a time. For example, although there seems to be an agreement that P277 and P278 have already been tendered, there is no such confirmation as regards P276. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't know anything -- we don't have any information with regard to P276 or at least an explanation by Mr. Di Fazio why it's not being tendered. In other words, are you renouncing to this document? MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that item 7 on the annexure, P276, is already in evidence as Exhibit P276.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have 276, Mr. Siller?

I don't know whether having him mentally occupied for so many long hours - in other words, the entire morning with you, and then the entire afternoon with us - could be counter-productive or not, but this is something that you are, and possibly the Victims and Witnesses Unit, better placed, better positioned than we are, because we don't know the gentleman. We don't -- I'm saying this because you're telling me that last time he was not feeling well and had to return. So I don't want to do anything or choose anything that at the end of the day in the bottom line would be counter-productive. That's number one. You should be in a better position. Secondly, I'm not quite sure a hundred per cent whether for the Hadzihasanovic Trial Chamber this would be possible, because the Chamber usually does not decide without consulting the parties. And although the Prosecution most of the time for the Prosecution it is possible, for the Defence it may not always be possible and we may find a problem there. So let's start from for the time being leave it there and explore these two possibilities. And you will then tell me at the next break or after the next break the position of the Trial Chamber, I suppose, we will need to reserve. But I mean it's no use trying to draw blood. If necessary, we'll have to adjourn this witness to Thursday. Certainly what is out of the question is that you start the examination of the witness tomorrow and then you continue the briefing after. I mean, that's out of the question. We will not tolerate it for sure. But we will -- if needs be, have to adjourn until Thursday. It's not going to be -- I mean, there are motions in this trial that we have received and that we will need to read, one of which is very lengthy. So it's not going to be a major setback if we have to adjourn by one day. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we'll deal with that after the next break. In the meantime, I also -- because one of the reasons I mentioned this this morning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a further problem. One of us has got problems with tomorrow afternoon, tomorrow afternoon. So there's no point in pursuing that matter any further with the Hadzihasanovic Trial Chamber, Mr. Siller. All right? So it's a question of whether -- the only thing that could happen is if the victims and units give their consent that you brief this man, this person -- I don't know, What time is he arriving?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: , Your Honour, the plane will arrive at 7.45 this evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Forget it. Forget it. Anyway, we'll have a confirmation of everything and then we'll decide after the next break. All right. Thank you. And the other thing I wanted to mention is when I asked you, Mr. Wubben, whether you wanted to change anything from this list, this list was compiled before I asked my legal officer to inform you that there will not be a sitting on Wednesday because of the visit to the Queen, and here you have Wednesday set down as a sitting during which Mr. Radic would be testifying, and the witness number 23, with witness number 24 testifying on Friday. As it is, it can't remain like that, and if necessary, please make sure that one of these witnesses, 23 or 24, stays wherever he is coming from and not be brought over unnecessarily and have to spend here an entire week in The Hague. All right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. To be clear to you, this is -- this schedule, this new schedule, is drafted after the information that Wednesday will not be a sitting day. That's why the 12th of January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I see it, if you want a suggestion on the part of the Bench, but it's just a suggestion, we're not interfering at all or pretending to interfere with the order of witnesses as you envisage it. Witness number 23 you had anticipated would testify over two days, while witness 24 would testify only in one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: 23, Your Honour. 23 one day and 24 two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have changed them already. Okay. Okay. Okay. That's what I was going to change. Yeah. That's what I was going to change. Okay. So that's not a problem. So let's proceed with the cross-examination now, or start with the cross-examination, Mr. Jones. You know what the procedure is, Ms. Manas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just by way of explanation, two points. Firstly, that we haven't actually received the physical exhibits from P271 onwards at this point, and so we reserve our position once we've received the physical exhibits and reviewed them to raise any points arising from reviewing those documents. That's the first point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And secondly, just to explain that when Ms. Manas last testified, she was the first witness, and I think we were all taken somewhat by surprise by her replacing Dr. Gow, and since then obviously there are matters which we've investigated and so I'm going to be reviewing matters raised or exhibits which were tendered on that occasion as well. I'm going to revisit certain items particularly because that also throws light on our objections to items in annex 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't suppose there is any objection from the Prosecution on that. The only problem that could arise is if Ms. Manas is prepared or not to answer these -- at least prepared -- it's not a question of whether she is willing. Whether she is prepared or not. Because you may be taking her by surprise on this. So the position is that if at any time you need to consult again those documents or your testimony, et cetera, or require time to verify, check things, just ask us and we will make sure that you will be given the -- all the opportunity. I mean, she is available at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We did provide the Prosecution when Ms. Manas was last listed to be a witness with a list of exhibits which we intended to use and that provided an opportunity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I meant to say is that she may be caught unaware today, and if that is the case then obviously you are perfectly entitled to put the question and if she is not in a position to answer, then we will postpone that matter until later.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Jones:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, first of all, just to be clear about your position in the Office of the Prosecutor, can you confirm that you're acting team leader of team 9 which is the Muslim leadership team?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the Naser Oric investigation has been and is being conducted by the Muslim leadership team?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've been assigned to that team since 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Team leader as of August last year?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, first just some general questions about the systems used by the OTP. Firstly about ERNs. Now, ERNs are eight-digit numbers, and they appear to be broken into two groups of four quite often, if not all the time. My question is: Do the first four digits denote that the document was seized from a particular collection? And to give an example, 0207, the 0207 prefix, that's the Sokolac collection; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yeah. If it came in during the same period it will naturally have the sequential date stamp numbers for that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll go slowly for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think that answers the question. What I mean to say is this: That for you, as a member of the Office of the Prosecution in charge of a team of investigators, if I tell you, Ms. Manas, I would like to refer you to document with B/C/S ERN number 00305702, that 0030, does it automatically bring to your mind a source of information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when I say 0030, you know exactly what I'm talking about, which collection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That answers your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is a record kept of which prefixes correspond to which collection?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And since we are at this, I mean it's just out of curiosity more than anything else, and that's also because I'm trying to be logical. Can you explain to me why the first four digits of the ERN number changes from B/C/S to English, it doesn't remain the same? In other words, why is it that, for example, with regard -- let's take P274. This comes from the collection 0030, and in the B/C/S it is 0030. In English, it is also 0030, as it should be. But then if you look at P273, the first four digits in the B/C/S ERN is 0027, but in English it is 0040. Why does it change?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it changes -- well, original number was given to it and when it's translated, another set of numbers is given to it. And in this case it retains the same number, I can't answer that, but I see it's got ET, means English translation, so no new number was given to it. They retain the same ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but my question is: Why isn't the first four digits which denote or point at the source of information remain the same, are not retained also in the English language? Because logically, that's how I would expect it to be. I mean, I wouldn't expect the last four digits to be the same as well, because obviously the length would -- of the translation or -- would vary from the original. As far as the source of information, why does it change? Because doesn't it create more confusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Okay. But the fact is that it seems that sometimes it changes, sometimes it is retained.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It seems there are those two situations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A question or two on IIFing and MIIFing. You told us last time you testified about IIF and MIIF forms, and you told us that when and MIIF form or an IIF form is compiled it's done electronically; that's right?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I take it, then, that they're searchable electronically as well?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can put in name of a person and find all the MIIFs or IIFs referring to that person?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's something you would routinely do to find prior statements by witnesses?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or you can enter a word like "Kravica" and you'll see all the IIFs which have the word in that description?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One preliminary question: We saw this morning that P295 in your annex 2 corresponds to P162 in your annex 1. I don't know if you have annex 1 with you, your previous -- annex to your previous declaration.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to make it available to the witness. Registrar, please. And we don't have it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but we don't have it available because we were not aware that you were going to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if this will show in P261, but you'll no doubt have this information. Isn't it right that the seizure details are different in fact for P162 and P295 and that P162 was seized by Mr. Tedder, 295 by Ms. Gilleece, if I'm pronouncing the name correctly?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Could you refer to the pre-trial number please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One moment. 238. Yes, 238 is P162.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Are we doing annex 1 or 2?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Annex 1.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: The pre-trial number, sorry, again?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: 238. I'm sorry. I've got something which doesn't -- it's not complete, so...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not terribly important point. Perhaps it's something you can check. Perhaps it's something which needn't detain us now, but our information is that the seizure details are actually different for those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a problem. MR. DI FAZIO: Confidentiality, is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. It's under seal. 262 is under seal. [Microphone not activated] I apologise. I apologise. What's being called in question is the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not the details. So we don't need to put it on the ELMO. The thing is this: In order for us to be able to follow properly, since we don't have the previous annex available as yet, we are still waiting for it, perhaps you can give the details as to the source as it appears from the previous annex and as it appears ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's number 238 on the pre-trial exhibit number, P162, and the information is that Steve Tedder seized that conduct from Colonel Rajko Sarenac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are we talking of 162 or 262?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Previously when it was -- when Ms. Manas was -- or Mr. Di Fazio was dealing with this, we're talking of pre-trial exhibit number 136, which was supposed, according to annex 2, to become Exhibit number P295. It's not being tendered today because we were told that it has already been tendered as P162. Now, that is the position. Now you mention P262.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, I didn't mention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not you. Mr. Siller did. So that we need to clarify first, whether we're talking of 162 or 262. Because if the document which is covered by confidentiality is 262 and not 162, we don't have that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Everyone is entitled to make mistakes, but not too many. Not too many. It's like dogs. Every dog is allowed one bite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 162. All right. Now, you need to explain to us according to annex 1 or the previous annex what was the declared source of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. It's annex 1, pre-trial number 238, P162 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why is it 238?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's the pre-trial exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But then it's not the same one, because the pre-trial exhibit number doesn't change; no?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, 238 is P162 and the information is that Steve Tedder seized the document from Colonel Rajko Sarenac. P295, annex 2 says that the document was seized by Eileen Gilleece.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What is the ERN number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That tallies with this. But according to pre-trial exhibit -- sorry, according to annex 2, the pre-trial exhibit number of that document is 136 and not 238.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There seem to be two pre-trial exhibit numbers as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could well be that one was tendered by Mr. Tedder and one was tendered Eileen --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't pursue that. I'd be grateful if Ms. Manas could check because we are concerned if seizure details are incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you get the point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps you can check and if there is any substantial important information that you could give us, you will give it to us, otherwise forget it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To return to annex 1, P261?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P261 is what was referred to as Sanja's list. I'm going to need to ask Ms. Manas about items on that spreadsheet, so ... I want to ask you about number 32, which is P17. The description is report of Ilija Ivanovic being brought into the military police station dated 16 January 1992.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have copies of that document. It's a Prosecution exhibit, so I won't distribute that at the moment. Yes, in fact, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just for the record, the ERN is 01239558 to 01239559. The seizure details that we have is that that was received from Jovcic Trivun liaison officer of Republika Srpska. That was the information provided in a previous spreadsheet. I think it doesn't appear on this.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you agreed last time, Mr. Trivun is just a liaison officer for the RS, so he's just a postman, in essence; he's not the source?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been able to establish who in fact provided that document or are you able to establish?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have an exhibit. With the usher's assistance. It's a statement of Dzenan Dzenanovic taken by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 13th of November, 2003. The ERN is 03465771. I'll direct your attention to paragraphs 15 and 16. You'll see there Mr. Dzenanovic was shown that document. And he says, paragraph 15: "I see my name also in the document number 01239558 in the first entry dated 16/01/93." And that's a document we just saw now, P17. And he goes on to say in paragraph 16: "I cannot identify or authenticate any of the signatures in these documents and also the contents. Even the signature below my name in document number 01239558 also, I'm not sure whether the signature is that of mine. The writing in the signature is different. I cannot identify the other signatures either. I've placed my signature on the reverse of all the documents which the numbers are entered above." Now, my question is: Are you aware that Dzenan Dzenanovic was shown this document and stated that one of the signatures was not his?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Now I'm aware, after reading this paragraph here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Office of the Prosecutor sent that document, P17, to the forensic document examiner, Dr. Fagel of the Netherlands Forensic Institute who testified here before us and that he examined the document and the signature against authentic specimen signatures provided by Dzenanovic and found that the signatures were probably not written by Mr. Dzenanovic, in other words, that they were forged or fake?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'm aware that the witness testified to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the signatures were examined by an expert?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that he found that the signature was probably not that of Mr. Dzenanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have that report as an exhibit, with the usher's assistance. Actually, at this stage if I could ask that Mr. Dzenanovic's statement be given a number. The relevant sections, in any event. It's paragraphs 15 and 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We only have the English version. I suppose that's the one you're interested in because the other one wouldn't carry his signature in any case. So this document which starts with ERN number 03465769 and runs through and includes 03465774 is being tendered by the Defence and admitted as -- marked as Defence Exhibit D --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, D139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 139. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you now have in front of you the report of Dr. Fagel March 2004? The ERN is 03594904. And I'll direct your attention to page 2 of 7 of that report, first of all, which is 03594905. And we see there that the ERN document with the ERN 01239558 was Q1, questioned signature, five from the bottom. And we will see that signature in appendix 2, which is ERN 0359416. And the conclusions on page 5 of 7, ERN is 03594908: "In view of the results of the examination, I conclude that the questioned signatures Q1," that's the one we've looked at, "Q2 and Q7 were probably not written by D. Dzenanovic." So you have a record of those matters?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That document, P17, despite being found probably to be a forgery, in any event, probably not to have been signed by the purported signatory, is still put being forward as a Prosecution exhibit, isn't it, P17? I'm not sure if the transcript has got your answer. Yes, P17 is still a Prosecution in this case. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think she should be the one to answer that. If it's in the record, it's in the record, and if it's not in the record, or if the Prosecution have withdrawn it or wants to withdraw it, that's another matter, but it's not the witness who will answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you this: Is it Prosecution's policy to continue to use documents as exhibits when the author says the signature has been forged and that's confirmed by expert evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you in a position to answer that question? Do you answer for the Prosecutor or not? Do you establish --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to answer that question, Your Honour. MR. DI FAZIO: And furthermore, we haven't heard anything from Dzenan Dzenanovic who got his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I wanted to correct something that the witness said because she said he hasn't testified. He's made a statement but...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you're at investigator in the Office of the Prosecutor. Generally you wouldn't want to prosecute someone on the basis of forged documents, would you?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the sort of information that signatures might have been forged is in fact troubling to the Prosecution and is something that you would want to investigate? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, there's no -- unless the statement says it's not his signature at the bottom. You have no evidence as to how whoever appended that signature at the bottom of the document came to do so. That's as far as the statement will take you, unless I'm wrong. He says it's not my signature at the bottom of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is not his signature and the document has actually been confirmed by a forensic document examiner. MR. DI FAZIO: The Forensic examiner says it's probably not his.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, most of this is argumentation. I mean, it's submissions basically, and I don't think it's -- you can expect the investigators are investigators. They do not establish the policy of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, the point is this: The following question which I was going to put to Ms. Manas is whether there's been an investigation into this matter and the purpose of putting these questions is to establish for Your Honours why we have such grave reservations about documents and it's not simply a question of looking at it document by document but the prosecutorial policy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not in question, Mr. Jones, that has never been in question and you are perfectly entitled to put these questions that you have just referred to to the witness but then you can only expect the witness to tell so much from that witness, from this witness, I mean. Not beyond that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, has there been an investigation into who provided, who the sources of this document, given that, as you said, Jovcic Trivun is just a postman and not the source?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'd like to state to the court that I didn't investigate this case. I only came on board as I said in my first testimony from the 1st of September and what transpired during the Oric investigation is that what I can tell you about. So I don't know the full nature, whether the signature forgery has been investigated, but I do know that reports have been submitted to the forensic expert for further investigations and investigators obtained statements, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would ask that Dr. Fagel's report be given a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Hasn't this already been given a number? No. So this document, which starts with ERN number 03594904 and finishes with 03594922 is being tendered and admitted -- tendered by the Defence and admitted and marked as Defence Exhibit D140. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one further matter on Mr. Dzenanovic's statement. We saw in the last sentence at paragraph 16, you don't need to refer to it, but that he signed the reverse of all the documents that he was shown. Isn't it right that it's OTP practice that when an investigator or lawyer shows a document to a witness and the witness comments on it, that then the witness is asked to sign the document for purposes of identification?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, moving to another subject. That document, P17, was supplied by the Republika Srpska bureau for cooperation with the ICTY, at least as the intermediary. And it's right, isn't it, that that bureau supplied a quantity of documents in this case?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you told us last time you testified that the OTP keeps track of sources of documents that are impeached in some way, and I'll read back what I asked you and what you said. I asked: "Do you also keep track of sources which have been impeached, let's say someone, a person who has provided documents and found to be untrustworthy, is he then blacklisted or somehow you keep track of the fact that the person has provided false or dubious documents?" I said: "Is that something that you do?" And you said: "Yes, we do." My question is: Has the RS bureau for cooperation with the ICTY been noted as an untrustworthy source?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that in 2002, the Republika Srpska government or department prepared a report into the Serb massacres of Bosnian Muslims in Srebrenica in July 1995? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That report also covers events in the enclave in 1992, 1993, including events which are the subject of this indictment, by way of background to the report. Are you aware that that report scandalised the international community by its distortion of the truth?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't have the report in front of me and I can't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that it was considered scandalous in its representation of events in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer that question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Could I have the usher's assistance. There's an exhibit which we'd like to pass up, and it's a six-page office of the High Representative, OHR BiH media roundup, setting out all the reactions to the RS report, as well as a page from Voice of America reporting the OHR's reaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that has also, to be fair, been superseded by subsequent declarations; no?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it has. But I want to focus, first of all, on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are perfectly entitled to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours can read through the reactions in your own time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be marked as Exhibit -- Defence Exhibit D141. And that's -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours can read the document in your own time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have read it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I have come across this already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just draw your attention, Ms. Manas, to some sections of this media roundup.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, would you please make pauses between questions and answers and read slowly when you read.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going too fast. In fact, I'm going to put the channel on B/C/S so that I can check it. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First page, second paragraph, we see that Miletic of the RS bureau for cooperation with the ICTY said: "The main purpose of the statement is to reveal the whole truth about the crimes in the Srebrenica area." And then if we see further down first page, fourth paragraph, Paddy Ashdown, the High Representative, his reaction condemning the report, said: "Srebrenica was not the only massacre in Bosnia and Herzegovina between 1992 and 1995. It was Europe's worst massacre since the Second World War. Pretending it didn't happen is an insult to people of all ethnic groups in BiH. If the accounts given in the media are correct, the report published today is so far from the truth as to almost not be worth dignifying a response. It is tendentious, preposterous, and inflammatory." And then finally, I would refer you to page 4, second paragraph. The comments of Graham Blewitt, formally the deputy Prosecutor of this Tribunal. And he says: "The Hague Tribunal Prosecution office, as well as the international community, has been embittered by that scandalous and shameful report in which the reliable and comprehensive evidence presented before the Tribunal have been totally ignored." Obviously, you worked under Graham Blewitt, as the former deputy Prosecutor, as your boss. Are you aware that he made those comments about the report or comments like them?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Now I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That didn't lead you or others to note the RS bureau was a questionable source, as an unreliable source of material, the fact that the report was condemned in those terms?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your question, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it. The fact that the RS government produced a report on Srebrenica which was described as scandalous and shameful, preposterous and inflammatory, isn't that something which would or did lead the OTP to note the RS bureau as an unreliable, as an untrustworthy source?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can't answer that. I'm not in a position to answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do it differently. How autonomous are you in your investigations? Do you take instructions? Do you receive instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You do. Did you ever receive instructions not to rely any further on the Republika Srpska as a reliable source of information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Never. Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That answers your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it the fact that the Office of the Prosecutor has gone further and taken the position in pleadings before this Tribunal that the report is so scandalous that the government of Republika Srpska can no longer be considered a serious source for any purposes? Are you aware of that position having been taken?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have a new exhibit. It's a filing by the Prosecution in Blagojevic, dated 12 November 2002. Essentially, the Prosecution response to Mr. Blagojevic's application for provisional release. Page 2 is missing. It just came out that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd refer you, Ms. Manas, to paragraphs 13 to 16 of that response, which concern the September 2002 report. It starts by referring to paragraph 14, starting with the words "the government of the Republika Srpska is obviously neither willing nor able to learn; rather, it sets out to perpetuate myths and lies, in sharp contrast with the very reason why this Tribunal was established. It is remarkable and unfortunate that this report carries the name of the very office that is supposed to facilitate the work of the ICTY." Then at paragraph 16: "The fact that the RS is still capable of publishing such gross propaganda seven years after the end of the war in Bosnia lends further support to the Prosecution's contention that the government of the RS is not serious in joining the international community." Sorry. I'll slow down for translation. I'm not sure if they caught the rest of that. I'll read it again: "The fact that the RS is still capable of publishing such gross propaganda seven years after the end of the war in Bosnia lends further support to the Prosecution's contention that the government of the RS is not serious in joining the international community and cannot be relied upon in any serious matter." I'll just firstly just that this document be given a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be Defence Exhibit marked D142.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, my question is: Isn't it apparent from that that the position of the OTP at least has been that the RS government cannot be relied upon in any serious matter? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I object to that question because that's not what the documentation says. It's not what the submission says, first of all. If you read it, it says, paragraph 16: "The Prosecution's contention that the government of the RS is not serious in joining the international community and cannot be relied upon in any serious matter in this case guarantees related to the Srebrenica accused." Furthermore, the other commentary from the OHR relating to -- or that commentary relates to the report about the events in Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've already addressed the 1995 issue. And Ms. Manas agreed that -- MR. DI FAZIO: How does it relate back to the principle, I assume the principle object of Mr. Jones and the Defence, namely, to throw doubt on the authenticity of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. Manas has already agreed that the report goes back to 1992, 1993, so I don't know if Mr. Di Fazio wasn't listening, but that's what she said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you think you're going to get from Ms. Manas? I mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate the point Your Honour is making. The fact is there are grave concerns we have about documents and sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's perfectly understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: There are various ways in which we can make those known to Your Honours. One is by filing motions, as we've done. The other is through the testimony of Ms. Manas, who is tendering a large number of exhibits and in certain matters perhaps she can assist, in other matters perhaps not. For our part we consider this is appropriate use of Ms. Manas to ask her about the OTP's policy and practice with respect to questionable sources. In answer to the other submission made by Mr. Di Fazio, the Prosecution's contention clearly stated in paragraph 16 is that the government of the RS cannot be relied upon in any serious matter. That's precisely what is stated. Then the Prosecution goes on to say specifically in this case they can't be trusted in relation to guarantees. But the main contention of the Prosecution is that the government of the RS cannot be relied upon in any serious matter. My point is this trial is a serious matter. How can the RS government be relied upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But the whole thing boils down to one basic issue, or not one; more than one, but there are two or three basic issues. Number one is this: That Ms. Manas is not the right person to answer that question. Ms. Manas will do as she is told. She will investigate and basically her duty is to collect all the intelligence, all the information that she can obtain. Then there will be others who will evaluate that information and decide whether to give any weight to those pieces, bits of information, and present them as evidence. And also the last but certainly not least consideration is, irrespective of what is written in this Prosecution consolidated response, the Blagojevic trial, at the end of the day, what is important is whether the Prosecution still continues to receive and accept information from Republika Srpska, whether it continues to attach importance or weight to the information from Republika Srpska and whether it continues to make use of that information in trials. Because saying this in this response is one thing, and operating then and translating your beliefs into practice is another. I mean -- and I don't think you can get the information or the right answer from Ms. Manas. I mean, you probably can get it from Mr. Wubben or Mr. Di Fazio or Ms. Sellers or from Ms. Del Ponte herself, not from Ms. Manas. I think Ms. Manas would end into serious trouble if she comes across pieces of information that are supplied from Republika Srpska and decides on her own steam that she will not even accept those and she will not even introduce them into the dossier that then others have to evaluate for the purpose of investigations and prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She will have to do as she is told.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Manas testified on the last occasion that the OTP keeps track of questionable sources, so my questions were designed to establish whether, in light of these events, the OTP had ever noted the RS government or bureau as a questionable source. And it's where will to make sure to Your Honours why we approach documents with such caution because if the Prosecution says in one case the RS bureau cannot be relied upon in any serious matter and in this trial, a serious matter, they are being relied upon in a very big way for documentary evidence, that will explain in part to Your Honours our reservations. So on this subject, in any event, I can move to the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: At the end of the day, it's not the Prosecution who is going to decide whether they carry any weight or not. It's we that will need to decide, putting everything in the basket, which will not be a simple exercise or an easy exercise at all. I mean, I can assure you. I mean, all the indications are there that we are going to have a difficult exercise at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour. And the question of sources is obviously a matter of weight to be attached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Everything that carries weight will be considered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, we've seen Dejan Miletic in your annex, item 116, in fact, of your annex 1, P262. And Dejan Miletic provided the whole rules of the road case against Naser Oric to the OTP, didn't he? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll pass up the next exhibit. We have a memorandum dated 4th of March, 2004 from ICTY investigator to the ICTY rules of the road unit. The ERN is RR321797. Closing the rules of the road case against Naser Oric. Paragraph 1 there. And then on the next page, we see the cover letter signed by Dejan Miletic. RR321795.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So looking at that, Ms. Manas, can you confirm that Mr. Miletic sent "statements of witnesses, records, and other documents" as evidence against Naser Oric to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: From this document, I can say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll ask if this document can be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be D143.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that regard, I'd also like to show you another exhibit, which is the transcript of an interview with Dejan Miletic on the 10th of March, 2004, on the Deutsche Welle Bosnian programme. In Bosnian and in English, which follows the B/C/S. And I'll just draw your attention to the first page of that interview. The journalist Sabrina Hodzic [phoen] says: "What happened with the materials that the RS secretariat for dialogue with the Tribunal sent to The Hague so far?" Miletic replied: "Well, The Hague Tribunal at that time there was still the bureau for cooperation with The Hague Tribunal, addressed the government of Republika Srpska and requested their assistance in conducting investigation against Naser Oric. We provided them certain assistance there. We submitted certain documents and then The Hague Tribunal brought the indictment." I'll stop there. So it's right, isn't it, that many of the documents used in this case against Naser Oric were provided by Dejan Miletic and the RS bureau for cooperation?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can't really answer that. I'm not sure if most of the documents that are used in this trial proceedings are from him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Dejan Miletic was removed from his position as head of the RS secretariat for relations with the ICTY by the High Representative, Paddy Ashdown, among other things, for document concealment? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: ... Exhibit which is the decision removing Dejan Miletic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This will be, first of all, D144, this interview with Dejan Miletic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now for the decision which you should have in front of you, would you please look at that document, and in particular to the actual decision to remove Dejan Miletic, role in obstructing the investigations into events in Srebrenica. And it's the last two pages. On the third page, the bottom, the bottom paragraph: "The report," and that's of the commission for investigation of events in and around Srebrenica, "makes abundantly clear that Mr. Miletic failed in his duties, indeed it may be concluded from the report that the secretariat over which he presided staged on obfuscation and obstruction which hindered the commission's ability to discharge its mandate effectively." And further down: "The report concludes that the secretariat," that's the secretariat over which Mr. Miletic presided, "actively engaged in document concealment." Now, if that information came to the attention of the Office of the Prosecutor, you would consider it pretty serious, wouldn't you? Active engagement and concealment would be a cause for concern?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it's right that Mr. Miletic is not kept on any blacklist by the OTP as a questionable source for documents, in light of his removal?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of. There might be, but I'm not aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document will be D145.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Moving to another area. If you look at your annex 1, pre-trial exhibit number 80, which is P65, perhaps the record of an on-site investigation of the death of Jakob Djokic dated 9 March 1993. Do you see that? Now, we're going to distribute copies of that document. The ERN is 02075762. That document, first, the ERN 02075762, I think you agreed with me earlier that 0207 is the Sokolac collection.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know the numbers offhand. If you say, I would take it as so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd like to pass up actually another exhibit, while we're with this one, which is the index to the Sokolac collection CD.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if you've seen similar indexes like these to the CDs of collections, in this case, the Sokolac collection, this document, Ms. Manas. In this index, if you look three lines down, number 3, document number 3, you have 02075760 to 02075762. Now, that's one document, is it not? And this document which we have as P65 is the last page of that document.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to refer to this index for a bit longer, so I'd ask that to be given an exhibit number, first of all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we start with the two pages, one in B/C/S, bearing ERN number 0 --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's already P65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's already P -- and that's -- bearing ERN number 02075762. And the English version having number 03038194. These have already been tendered and admitted in evidence and marked as Prosecution Exhibits P65. So then the chart or the index that consists of three pages and which deals in total with 104 items of documentation and to which reference has been made by Mr. Jones in his last question to Ms. Manas, is being tendered and admitted in evidence as Defence Exhibit D146. Is it good? Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
