utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And we'd in fact like to pass up copies of the full document, 02075760 to 02075762 just to see it in its complete form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Entirety, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look on the last page of the document you've just been handed, Ms. Manas, P65, it's the last page, appears to be signed by Dr. Avdo Hasanovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that Dr. Hasanovic was shown this document and that he stated that the signature was not his, on P65? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd like to pass up the statement by Dr. Hasanovic, in which he deals with ... Paragraph 67 of the statement given in March 2004. He says there: "I've been shown an original document bearing ERN 02075762 by investigator Nasir. The signature on the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Paragraph 67, which is on page 10. "The signature on the document is not mine. I do not remember examining this patient myself. He might have been examined by my colleagues. I want to mention here that the seal on this document might have fallen to the Serbs at the fall of Srebrenica in July 1995. There is a possibility that the Serbs prepared this document."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do your records show or are you aware of whether this possibility was investigated, that the Serbs had seized official stamps upon the fall of Srebrenica and prepared documents?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't that an allegation which should have been taken seriously and investigated?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a serious allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The thing is this: When did you read this statement by Avdo Hasanovic? When did you come across it the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the investigator came back from the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And wouldn't it have fallen under the competence of -- competence, jurisdiction, of your team to investigate such a matter, in other words, whether the Serbs had obtained, come into possession of stamps which they then used for the forging, falsification of documents? Wouldn't it have fallen under your competence or would you have referred it to your superiors for further instructions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that should have been done, but unfortunately I wasn't the acting team leader then and it didn't form part of this investigation then. So I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But was your team entrusted only with investigating the Muslim leadership or also other matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim leadership. But we had three other investigations which we were working on and I didn't work on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. One moment now, Mr. Jones, in order not to confuse matters. You have what was previously, we said, P65, which transpires to be only part of these three pages. Do you want to tender these three pages starting from 02075760?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will become Defence Exhibit D147. And then the statement by Avdo Hasanovic, you also want to tender, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. In any event, the relevant paragraphs which were referred to, not necessarily the whole statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When you tender, we are not going to look at the other matters, substitution of testimony for sure, definitely not. D147. This will be D147. This is why I keep repeating every now and then that we are professional Judges and you don't need to worry about -- did I make a mistake, Mr. Siller? Should it have been another number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This will be 148, sorry. This statement by Avdo Hasanovic will be 148. Okay. Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Dr. Hasanovic isn't going to be called as a witness in this case. Was he dropped as a witness after that statement from him was obtained, as a result of his stating that the signature on the document was not his?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this remains P65, Prosecution Exhibit P65, despite the fact Dr. Hasanovic has said that he thinks that his signature has been faked. You don't have to answer that. It's the same point as before. Now, that document was received, was it not, by Dan Perry from Major Ranko Todorovic, in the 5th Corps headquarters Sokolac; in other words, it's part of the Sokolac collection?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Is that what it says in my spreadsheet?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would say that's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to refer you to item 83 in your annex. It's P68. It's the record of on-site investigation of death of Dragan Ilic, dated 10 March 1993. Firstly, I'd like you to refer back to D146, the index to the Sokolac CD. Looking at the second document there, 02075763 to 02075765, again, P68 is part of that document, of that three-page document?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's the last page of that three-page document.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And again we have as an exhibit the full three-page document, which we'd ask to be given a Defence exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Registrar, could you check with the technicians and translators whether -- because we started at 10 to 11.00; no? 10 to 11.00. Whether they prefer -- we could go on to 12.30, as scheduled, or strictly speaking, we could also stop at 12.20, which would be the 1 hour and 30 minutes that we are allocated. But see what they prefer. Yeah, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We're just passing up, I think, copies of that three-page document and asking for an exhibit number. It should be D149.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have copies of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Then we go until 12.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That document, P68, also appears to be signed by Dr. Avdo Hasanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Is it P68 or P60 -- because what I have now is -- can you put it on the ELMO for a moment so that we check, please. Because what I have -- can you give us the ERN number, because I think we are --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In fact, what might assist, Your Honour, is there are two Prosecution exhibits in this three-page document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is 565.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So first page is 02075763.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. 565; no? 765.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: 5765 is P68. In fact, the prior page is P67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if you have Dr. Hasanovic's statements with you. If not, it doesn't matter. I'll read it to you.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, it can't be 67. Let's -- this document consists of three pages, like the previous one, which was then marked as P147. The first of these three pages is 02075763.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The next one is 02075764, and shows also that -- or denotes that it has become Prosecution Exhibit P67. And then we have a final page with the ERN number 02075765, which you are telling me is Prosecution Exhibit P68.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What about the first one? Does it form part of any -- of these two documents or is it an additional one?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's not a Prosecution exhibit. The three pages constitute one document in the Sokolac collection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. This is why I'm asking you. You are going to tender this as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what I want to make sure for the record, because I know the answer already, but for the record, I want it from you that the first page of these three pages does not form part of either P67 or P68.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And this document in its entirety now comprising, in other words, what is already P67 and P68, will become Defence Exhibit D149. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just refer back to Dr. Hasanovic's statement. As I say, you don't need to refer to it. I'll just simply read the relevant paragraph. Paragraph 68: "I've been shown an original document bearing ERN 02075765 by investigator Nasir. The signature on the document is not mine. I do not remember examining this patient myself." And at paragraph 65, Dr. Hasanovic also expressed doubts about 02075764. Again, my question, and I think you've answered it in relation to the other exhibit, this isn't something which was investigated, whether these documents were forged?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to some new items on your annex. We can dispense with that for the time being. I'd like to direct your attention to numbers 56 and 57 on your annex 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The previous one. And is this all mine or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's a question, really, about ERNs in that -- between those two exhibits, P41 and P42. You see the ERNs there, 01839701, is P41, and then 01840629 to 01840630 is P42. And both of those documents were taken by Steve Tedder from Colonel Saranac in Banja Luka on at the same place, same day?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: A document with an ERN falling between those two ERN numbers would be from the same source, wouldn't it, from Colonel Sarenac on the same day?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Same day. But when brought into the Evidence Unit it might not be the same time, so maybe that's why the numbers are so different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because I want to ask about document with ERN 01840522 and it's not a Prosecution exhibit, but my suggestion to you is that that would therefore be also from the Banja Luka collection and Colonel Sarenac because the ERN falls between P41 and P42, which are from that source, if you follow?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yeah, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Copies of that document, 01840552.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that this document was shown to Kasim Suljic, who is mentioned in that document, and that he cast doubt on the document's authenticity? We can probably now pass up a statement by Kasim Suljic, which I have copies for everyone. And it's paragraph 110 of that statement which is being passed around. Page 9, paragraph 110: "I have been presented with document ERN 01840522 to 10840522 [sic] I've never seen this document before now. If this is real, I should have been given a copy. I was never given this authorisation and I never carried out this action. I did not go to the supreme command in Sarajevo." So isn't it right Mr. Suljic gave a statement to the Prosecution saying in essence that that document was suspect. MR. DI FAZIO: With respect, he's not, if Your Honours please. He says he's never seen the document. He says if it was real he should have been given a copy. He says it was never given this authorisation. And he says he didn't go to the supreme command. Maybe Mr. Oric signed the document, didn't do anything with it. The conclusion that's being jumped to is too far, too big a stretch.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: "If this is real, I should have been given a copy." He wasn't given a copy, therefore, it's not real.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It says what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that investigated, the possibility that this document was not authentic?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd also draw your attention to paragraph 109 of the same statement. "I've been presented with document ERN 0211073, information in the letter depicts the situation but I do not recall the letter and I certainly did not write it." Isn't is it right from the ERN numbering of that document that it would fall between P82 and P83 in your annex? I don't know if you can see that. It's items 96 and 97. P82 is 02110276, P83, 02113315. So would it be right that that document falls between P82 and P83?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Which paragraph on the statement again, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 109. 02113073.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a record of the source of that document, 02113073? Or if you don't have it, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I don't have it front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you can find it for us on some other occasion. I would ask that this part anyway of Mr. Suljic's statement be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The previous document --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm not asking for that to be exhibited. It was purely as a visual aid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So this is not exhibited. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. Just so that I can follow this. I'm sorry, Your Honours, to interject. What's not being tendered? Is that 01840522?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. That's what I understood. MR. DI FAZIO: May I ask why that's not being tendered? It was cross-examined -- there was evidence led about the document, and the statement of Mr. Suljic will make really little sense unless we see the document. Surely it should be given an exhibit number. I'd press for its admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's simply that our case is that this document is completely false. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And provided that's clear, it can be exhibited. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand the purpose of -- and I quibble with that, but it's been touched upon, and I think for the sake of completeness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But you understand I cannot force the Defence to tender a document into exhibit. MR. DI FAZIO: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If they don't want to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: The point is taken because indeed it's true of some of the other documents which have been exhibited, provided it's obviously clear to everyone that we don't accept the authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it makes a lot of sense. MR. DI FAZIO: That's perfectly understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be D150 and the statement by Kasim Suljic will be D151, and the understanding is we'll only make use of the two paragraphs referred to, that is, paragraphs 109 and 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will need to stop at about one or two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I'm about to move to a new area, so we should really break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll stop here. We'll have a 25-minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to conclude within 30 minutes, if possible, if we make progress.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's better for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, if I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tomorrow we will not be sitting, Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: It is indeed about the announcement your Court made regarding the witness, and it's of importance for us to reschedule and take measures. That's why I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We will definitely. I mean, it doesn't make sense. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ms. Manas, I'm now going to ask you some questions which relate to documents purportedly signed by Dr. Pilav. You may know that he was listed as a witness a one point but he is no longer listed as a Prosecution witness. I want to start by directing your attention to item number 61, which is P46, in your annex 1. And the ERN is 02075703. The description is "notes from interrogation of prisoner Kostadin Popovic, dated 30 January 1993." And it was seized by Dan Perry from Major Todorovic. Now, looking again at this CD index to the Sokolac collection, document 22 is the full four-page document, isn't it, in which that page is found, 02075703 to 02075706?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And again, just so everyone can follow, we're going to pass up the four-page document as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, 02075703 is the first page. That's P46. I'm going to ask you about the last page, 02075706. That appears to be signed by Dr. Pilav. Now, are you aware that Dr. Pilav was shown that document at page and he cast doubt on the authenticity of it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. I read the documents that you gave the Prosecution that you were going to use against me, so I read his statement last night.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'd like to pass up copies of Dr. Pilav's statement. It's at paragraph 56 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see Dr. Pilav there stated: "I do not recall" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Paragraph 56.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I do not recall typing this report regarding Kostadin Popovic." ERN 02075706. "I find the report to have many illogical issues." And then he goes on to explain in that paragraph and in paragraphs 58 and 59 all of the anomalies of the document. Now, that document is from the Sokolac collection, isn't it, Ms. Manas?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Well, if it's in my seizure details as such, then I take it is that because I don't have the complaint to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at this complete document. It's four pages. The first page is P46, the next two pages don't appear to be exhibited, and certainly the last page is not an exhibit, is it, 02075706? You can take that from me if you don't have a record of that. That's not an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it right that in fact what's happened is Dr. Pilav has been dropped as a witness, and one of these pages is being exhibited as a Prosecution exhibit and the suspect pages are just being ignored?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know the reason for that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you have a four-page document as a matter of practice in the OTP, and one page of that appears doubtful for some reason or other, is it normal practice then to just use another page as a perfectly reliable Prosecution exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why are you expecting her to answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm asking about OTP practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but she is an investigator. She is not a Prosecutor. Later on when it's ripe, just throw it into Mr. Di Fazio's lap or Mr. Wubben's lap. I mean, it's ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Manas, you can answer this: On the CD of the Sokolac collection we see these four pages as one document. Who is it who decides what constitutes an exhibit? Is it you or is it lawyers from the OTP who decide?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Of course the investigator, he or she will check what's relevant and produce it to the Prosecutor, and from there the Prosecution decides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has there, if you know, been any serious investigation by the OTP into this particular anomaly, in other words, going back, for example, to Major Todorovic and saying: What's going on with these documents? Are they genuine? Why does the author say that he didn't sign it? Has there been anything of that nature been done?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to item 76, which is P61 on your annex.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. I believe it had been tendered.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The four pages starting with ERN 02075703 until -- and ending with 02075706 are being tendered by the Defence and admitted and marked as Defence Exhibits D152.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will also be asking for Dr. Pilav's statement to be exhibited, the relevant parts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Dr. Pilav's statement, which starts with ERN number 01171402 and consists of -- and ends with ERN number 01171416 is being also tendered by the Defence as an exhibit of theirs, and it's being admitted and marked as Defence Exhibit D153. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Just one -- it's a very minor matter, but just so that we're all on the same wavelength, so to speak. Mr. Jones mentions as he's tendering these documents in relation to the statement, I tender the statement, for example, of Dr. Pilav, the relevant portions. The Prosecution has no objection to his using the statement, but it would seek that all of the statement be tendered into evidence. I know what you've said regarding the content of the statement, but it may be that the date the statement was taken may become relevant and if we don't have the date at the front of the statement, it could cause difficulties later on. So just so that everyone is clear, the Prosecution has no objection so long as the entire statement is put into evidence. I'm well aware of all the other evidentiary issues relating to the other content of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think there's no problem with the whole statement, all of these statements, being physically put in together and of course we all understand that it's only a portion that's referring to the documents they've been shown which are being put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that's perfect. I took it to be like that in the first place in any case. But that's why I agree we are on the same wavelength. I mean, it's no problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we're looking at item number 76 in your annex 1, which is P61. And the ERN is 02075736. And the description is "handwritten notes from interrogation of prisoner Bogdan Zivanovic, dated 21 January 1993." It's right, isn't it, that that was also seized as part of the Sokolac collection?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: If you say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could refer you again to the index of the CD. At line 12, document 12, we have 02075735 to 02075737. And that's a document relating to Bogdan Zivanovic. So isn't it right again that this is, this P61, is again only one page of a larger document, a three-page document?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we'll pass up copies of that document. Now, the first page of that, 02075735 is P60. 5736 is P61. And then we're looking at the last page, 02075737. Now, if I refer you again to this statement by Dr. Pilav, he was shown, was he not, this page, 02075737, and he discussed it, and at paragraph 64: "I can tell you with certainty that I did not examine any dead bodies in 1992, 1993. I did not write these reports." And he's referred to a document referring to Bogdan Zivanovic. Now, again it's the same point, and perhaps you can't help us with it, but isn't what's happened is you have a three-page document. The first page, P61, the second, P61; the third page is the author who has cast doubt on the authenticity, and that's simply been pulled and discarded and the other two are being relied on as perfectly reliable documentary exhibits? That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: If you say so. I mean, I can't answer in more detail than that why, why it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Forgive my ignorance if what I'm saying is due to it, but you mentioned paragraph 64; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. And then if you go back to paragraphs 61 and 62, it's referring to the report on Bogdan Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but there's no reference to the specific document; no?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no, but it's clearly that document. In fact, it may even be annexed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because we don't even have a translation of this document, this last ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In our submission, this is the document. Perhaps there's -- the way of establishing it is looking at paragraph 60, where you see the ERN 02075737. Sorry, in fact, that's it. That is the ERN, paragraph 60. Yeah. Paragraph 60, one sees that that is the document that he's been shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: 737, I can see the name of Pilav, but on the other two pages, 35 and 36, what does it have to do with Pilav?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. 02075737, as you see, is signed by Pilav. This is a three-page document, as we see from the index to the Sokolac collection, and it consists of these three pages, 5735, 5736, 5737. And the point I was putting to Ms. Manas is that the last page has simply been torn off and discarded while relying on the other two pages as reliable documentary evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: But just to make sure. The statement of Dr. Pilav in P -- in D153 does not refer to P60, P61; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: No, it doesn't refer to P61. His signature isn't purportedly on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So your position is if you turn in document 737, you should also turn in 735 and 736, even if there is no internal connection between these pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. That's our submission, that that's how the Prosecution should proceed. We've passed up the exhibit which is all three pages together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Do you want to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this three-page document starting with ERN 02075735 and ending with ERN 02075737, the first two pages of which are already exhibits, Prosecution exhibits P60 and 61, is being tendered by the Defence as its own exhibit and is being received and marked as Defence Exhibit D154.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And finally, there's one more document that I'd ask you to look at, Ms. Manas, in this series, starting with the index to the Sokolac collection. It's at line 10 and it's the document 02075742 to 02075745. I'm going to refer to the person by the pseudonym. It's a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it right in this case too we have a four-page document, 02075743 is P62, and the other pages which refer to the death of the person, who is in fact alive, were not being tendered as Prosecution exhibits? Are you aware of that? First page, 02075742, the annotation at the bottom "buried in cemetery." The last page, report that someone has died. And in fact, this person is alive, died in prison. Because in fact, this person is alive and will be a witness in this case.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's in B/C/S, so I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: This is, in fact, the subject -- partly the subject of a motion, Your Honour, so in fact I won't dwell. I just wanted to get that document in its entirety in as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's better. The way you've been dealing with this I think is perfect. So this will be D155. Correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Moving to a different area, I want to ask you a question about a document which appeared item 103 of your first annex. And it's the ERN 02621257 to 02621260. And it's the description of attack on Rupovo Brdo, Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that is no longer a Prosecution exhibit. It was P86, but it's been withdrawn. I'd like to pass up copies of that document in order to ask you a question about it. This is in B/C/S. I'll ask you to look at the last page, where there are some signatures. And it's right, isn't it, that it appears to be signed by, among other people, by someone called Ramo Hodzic, and that's the second of three signatures at the bottom? Do you see that, Ramo Hodzic?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I see a name, Ramo Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll pass up the statement of Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you to look at paragraph 18 of that statement. He says there: "I've been shown an original document bearing ERN 02621257 to 02621260 by investigator Nasir. I've never seen this document previously. I was never involved in the preparation of this document. I was never involved in the preparation of any other documents like this one. In fact, I've never been part of the 28th Division." My question is: That document is no longer a Prosecution exhibit, but isn't it right that it's in the same format as documents which are still being put forward as Prosecution exhibits? And I'm referring to P87. If you look on 104 on your list. P88 and P89.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I've got copies of those.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you, Ms. Manas: Looking at the document which we just looked at with Mr. Hodzic's statement, and these three documents, they're all in the same form, aren't they; they're the same basic format? The headings are the same and we have signatures on the last page.

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: It appears to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you: Has there been any investigation in that respect into whether given that Mr. Hodzic says that the Rupovo Brdo document was false, maybe these other documents are false as well? Checked with the purported signatories in each case?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: I don't know. Sorry. I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a final couple of questions. Firstly, have you been able to determine since the last occasion when you testified what government department is in Sokolac or what agency is in Sokolac, the source of the Sokolac collection? I think you said it was the 5th Corps HQ, but do you have any further information about what agency is based there?

utterances.speaker: RACINE MANAS [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I didn't go further into looking at that. I didn't know I was supposed to. That was covered during the first testimony, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. We have some exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Start with the one which originally seems to have had the -- first of all, consists of four pages and originally had the sequential ERN number from 026 to 1257 to 02621260, but which also --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I think it was given a new ERN probably when the witness signed it and was shown it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
